summary: Inline round 7 review: three round 6 blockers are resolved; response classification is partially resolved. Offline reproductions found three remaining safety gaps involving pending-record deletion, automatic configure retries after 5xx responses, and unrecognized HTML account-stop signals. TypeScript validation passed. No live Instagram calls were made.

prior_blockers.title: Recursive Chrome-profile isolation still fails open
prior_blockers.evidence: Nonempty-profile reset failures now return ok:false, and recursive inspection failures also return ok:false (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/secure.ts:85, secure.ts:88, secure.ts:103). Offline mocked failures confirmed both paths reject isolation. auth.ts:240 requires isolation before launching Chrome at auth.ts:244. Native ACL mutation was not exercised.

prior_blockers.title: Overlapping manual unlocks can delete an active publisher's lock
prior_blockers.evidence: Each publisher now exclusively creates its own uniquely named claim, inspects competing claims, and releases only its own pathname (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/pending.ts:97, pending.ts:99, pending.ts:101, pending.ts:105). unlockStale removes only the previously inspected dead owner's uniquely named claim (pending.ts:129, pending.ts:130), eliminating replacement of the shared pathname involved in the prior race.

prior_blockers.title: Non-JSON response classification permits unsafe fallback and clears ambiguous publishes
prior_blockers.evidence: Challenge/login detection now precedes non-JSON 404 classification (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:269), and publish.ts:457 preserves pending state for 5xx account-stop responses. Offline checks confirmed both fixes. However, HTML challenge responses with status 200 or 403 still clear pending state and permit another publish (client.ts:278; publish.ts:457).

prior_blockers.title: Explicit false confirmation flags execute mutations
prior_blockers.evidence: Boolean assignments now parse true/1 as true, remove false/0 switches, and reject other values (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:89, main.ts:92, main.ts:93, main.ts:94). Offline CLI execution with --confirm=false --experimental=false remained a dry run with zero fetches; confirmed commands with --experimental=false were rejected before client creation.

strengths: Authenticated fetches enforce HTTPS and an allowlisted Instagram hostname, with redirects disabled. Origin overrides retain Instagram domain boundaries; GraphQL bundle fetches supply no cookies (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:211, client.ts:233; constants.ts:27; graphql.ts:85).

All eight write-command dry-run routes made zero fetches in an offline harness with mocked local media/storage. Experimental gating occurs before client creation, and every current write contract remains gated (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:130, main.ts:140, main.ts:145, main.ts:354, main.ts:358; publish.ts:23).

Cookie replacement secures an empty temporary file before writing credentials and renaming it over the destination. Storage failures throw unless the documented insecure-storage override is explicitly enabled (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/cookie-store.ts:120, cookie-store.ts:126, cookie-store.ts:127, cookie-store.ts:128; secure.ts:113, secure.ts:118).

Routine session output redacts cookie values, publish descriptions redact authentication headers, and GraphQL page tokens remain in memory (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:221; cookie-store.ts:177; publish.ts:313; graphql.ts:65).

Unreadable or corrupt pending state blocks publishing. Candidate matching never automatically resolves a record, and generic 5xx failures retain unresolved state (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/pending.ts:143, pending.ts:151; publish.ts:408, publish.ts:440, publish.ts:463).

The CLI has no like, follow, or DM commands; research caps are enforced. Default request pacing is 1500 ms, with an environment override (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:307, main.ts:313; constants.ts:54; client.ts:108).
TypeScript validation passed with --noEmit across implementation and tests.

blocking_findings.title: HTML account-stop responses below HTTP 500 still erase pending protection
blocking_findings.why: An HTML response does not establish whether configure committed. Clearing its pending record permits another publish despite uncertain server state, contradicting the plan's promise that HTML responses remain unresolved.
blocking_findings.evidence: Non-JSON challenge/login responses become checkpoint/not_logged_in errors without retaining response-format information. executeLocked treats those kinds as definitive whenever status is below 500, including HTTP 200. Offline execution returned HTML challenge responses with statuses 200, 403, and 404; two sequential publishes each reached configure, and no pending record remained. The equivalent 502 response correctly retained a record and blocked the second publish.

blocking_findings.title: A 5xx transcode-shaped response triggers automatic configure retries
blocking_findings.why: The pending safeguard does not prevent retrying an ambiguous configure request. A 5xx response must remain uncertain regardless of its body; treating it as permission to configure again undermines duplicate-post protection.
blocking_findings.evidence: classifyBody recognizes in_progress and transcode messages before checking status >=500. configure retries solely from the resulting error kind, video presence, and attempt count, without checking HTTP status. An offline video publish receiving HTTP 502 with {"status":"in_progress"}, followed by success, made two configure calls and cleared pending state. The plan explicitly promises that 5xx responses remain pending whatever their body.

blocking_findings.title: HTML feedback and wait signals still allow authenticated fallback
blocking_findings.why: Continuing endpoint discovery after an explicit restriction or rate-limit message adds requests to an account that should have stopped. The safety contract covers feedback_required and please-wait signals, not only challenge/login markers.
blocking_findings.evidence: Non-JSON handling detects challenge/login markers and HTTP 429 but does not inspect feedback_required or the please-wait message recognized by JSON classification. Other HTTP 200 HTML becomes unexpected_response, which permits read fallback. Offline responses containing <html>feedback_required</html> and <html>Please wait a few minutes before you try again.</html> each caused tryEach to call the second authenticated endpoint. Actual Instagram restriction-page formats remain unverified live.

open_questions: No live Instagram calls could be made. Payload acceptance, actual account-stop pages, transcode semantics, and deletion behavior remain unverified; all write contracts should retain their experimental status.

Bun was unavailable on PATH, and the full unit suite creates filesystem fixtures incompatible with this read-only environment. Runtime checks used Node TypeScript transformation, mocked network/storage, and accelerated retry timers; they do not establish full Bun-suite acceptance.
Native Windows ACL mutation and Chrome-profile reuse were not exercised. Recursive failure handling was verified with mocked icacls results.

Live acceptance remains weak: the read test accepts an empty posts array without asserting the source or pagination, and deletion verification checks absence from that feed without establishing its completeness (instagram-ai-plugin/test/live.test.ts:36, live.test.ts:38, live.test.ts:71, live.test.ts:72).
Credential redaction was checked in routine output and dry-run construction; malformed-cookie diagnostics under Bun were not exercised.
